name: Repairing Damaged Garage Drywall: Step-by-Step Restoration Process

step.name: Step 1: Identify and stop the source of damage
step.text: Find whether the damage stems from physical vehicle impact, exterior roof runoff, or a hidden plumbing leak above. Never proceed with repairs until active leaks are fully resolved.

step.name: Step 2: Inspect the wall cavity and remove compromised materials
step.text: Cut away swollen, crumbling, or mold-affected drywall back to the nearest sound wall studs using a utility knife. Remove damp insulation and inspect the interior wood framing for structural rot.

step.name: Step 3: Dry and clean the wall cavity completely
step.text: Allow the framing cavity to air out thoroughly using supplemental ventilation or dehumidification before hanging new materials. Applying drywall over damp studs traps moisture and causes future decay.

step.name: Step 4: Measure and cut matching fire-rated replacement board
step.text: Verify whether the existing wall requires 5/8-inch Type X gypsum board or standard drywall, and cut a replacement patch that fits snugly within the opening. Secure it to framing with proper drywall screws.

step.name: Step 5: Restore fire-rated seals around all penetrations
step.text: Apply approved fire-stopping sealant around any electrical boxes, gas pipes, or plumbing lines crossing the repaired area. Ensure no unsealed gaps remain between the utility line and the drywall edge.

step.name: Step 6: Apply joint tape and finish compound layers
step.text: Embed joint tape over all patch seams using setting-type joint compound, followed by finish coats feathered wide into surrounding surfaces.
